state:
Goal `core-process-and-4-more`. `Core\Process` is green. `Core\Process\Handle` has its class card, and `kill`, `readStdout`, `readStderr` and `writeStdin` have all their feature proofs. `wait` still owes everything but its card, and `HANDLE_WAIT_DOC` is still in the old voice. `Core\Process\Result`, `Core\Program` and `Core\Queue` are untouched and still in `CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD`.

The chain floor checks are green again: 59 goal records named the playbook selector `Tooling > a commit`, which opened two bullets once "A commit that narrows …" landed. They now name `Tooling > a commit message`.

`writeStdin` takes `bytes` only; a `string` does not compile (`E0401`), so its card and examples say `as bytes`. The Rust tests start this suite's own binary as the child: `SLEEPER` runs until killed, `ECHOER` copies its input to its error output until the input ends.

A Unix-only example is run by hand under WSL. Put the commands in a script under `.agent-tmp/` and start it with `wsl.exe -- bash -lc "bash <script>"`. In the script, build with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/var/tmp/nvs-target-wsl cargo build` from `/mnt/d/mwl`, run `/var/tmp/nvs-target-wsl/debug/nvs run --config <dir>/nvs.toml <file>`, and write the `.out` with Write from what it printed. The attacks and benches run on both platforms: they pick `/bin/sh` or `cmd.exe` by `Core\Path::SEPARATOR`; a Windows child that reads and discards its input is `cmd.exe /c "findstr /v zzzz >nul"`. `bytes` has no `.` operator: `Core\Bytes::repeat` builds a large value. A perf figure goes stale whenever `process.rs` changes: `bun nv proofs --record-perf --only '<member>'` re-measures one.
